title: Oxygen — Replacement of the Passenger Chemical Oxygen Generators by the Twenty-Two Minute Unit

issue.reason: Initial issue of the twenty-two minute passenger oxygen generator retrofit bulletin.

abstract: Cabin retrofit replacing the twelve minute passenger oxygen generators by twenty-two minute units with the matching hose set, opening the extended high terrain and over-water routes several operators have asked for.

sections.planning_reason: Three operators moved this type onto routes crossing high terrain where the depressurisation escape profile takes longer than the twelve minute generator supports, and each of them accepted an operational restriction to keep the route. A fourth asked for the same capability for an over-water sector. The twelve minute generator is also the second most common cabin item found expired at a scheduled inspection, because its shelf life does not match the rest of the passenger service unit contents and produces an out-of-phase replacement task.
sections.description: The bulletin replaces every passenger service unit generator with the twenty-two minute unit, replaces the mask hose set to suit the higher initial flow and replaces the firing actuator in each unit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Take the cabin out of service and drop the passenger service unit panels along the full cabin length. Do the removal task AMM-C-35-20-11-000-015-A for each generator and discharge it under the operator's hazardous material procedure. Install the twenty-two minute generator D3520111793165 in each unit. Install the hose kit D3520115531984 and replace the outboard hose D3520117654228 at every second row from row 4 aft, as listed on sheet 2 of the accomplishment instructions. Install the firing actuator D3520120132145 and check the pin travel. Secure the longer hose run above the ceiling panel with loop clamps LN551613K3. Install the filter sub-assembly D3520127667247 at each manifold. Do the pull test at three sampled units and record the result. Close the panels, do the cabin pressure integrity check and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00137 to MSN C00612 fitted with the twelve minute generator. Aircraft from MSN C00612 onward are already at the standard. One aircraft in a freighter conversion is excluded. A mixed installation within one passenger service unit is prohibited.
sections.material_note: Kit K3520-2002-01 is supplied per cabin and contains the generators, the hose set, the actuators and the clamp set. Lead time is twenty-four weeks and the generator is the long-lead item. Removed generators are not returned and must be discharged and disposed of by the operator.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience, and before the operator plans a route whose depressurisation escape profile exceeds twelve minutes.

title: Oxygen — Replacement of the Passenger Chemical Oxygen Generators by the Twenty-Two Minute Unit

issue.reason: Outboard hose row list published per cabin layout and the fitted layout made an input to the kit order.

abstract: Cabin retrofit replacing the twelve minute passenger oxygen generators by twenty-two minute units, with the long hose row list given per cabin layout because the galley position decides which rows need it.

sections.planning_reason: Three operators moved this type onto routes crossing high terrain where the depressurisation escape profile takes longer than the twelve minute generator supports, and each of them accepted an operational restriction to keep the route. A fourth asked for the same capability for an over-water sector. The twelve minute generator is also the second most common cabin item found expired at a scheduled inspection, because its shelf life does not match the rest of the passenger service unit contents and produces an out-of-phase replacement task.
sections.description: The bulletin replaces every passenger service unit generator with the twenty-two minute unit, replaces the mask hose set to suit the higher initial flow and replaces the firing actuator in each unit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Establish the cabin layout fitted to the aircraft from the cabin configuration record and select the matching row list on sheet 2; there is one list per layout and they are not the same. Take the cabin out of service and drop the passenger service unit panels along the full cabin length. Do the removal task AMM-C-35-20-11-000-015-A for each generator and discharge it under the operator's hazardous material procedure. Install the twenty-two minute generator D3520111793165 in each unit. Install the hose kit D3520115531984 and replace the outboard hose D3520117654228 at every row on the selected list. Install the firing actuator D3520120132145 and check the pin travel. Secure the longer hose run above the ceiling panel with loop clamps LN551613K3. Install the filter sub-assembly D3520127667247 at each manifold. Do the pull test at three sampled units and record the result, and include one unit from a long hose row in the sample. Close the panels, do the cabin pressure integrity check and record the embodiment together with the layout the row list was taken from.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00137 to MSN C00612 fitted with the twelve minute generator. Aircraft from MSN C00612 onward are already at the standard. One aircraft in a freighter conversion is excluded. A mixed installation within one passenger service unit is prohibited. The row list for the outboard hose is layout dependent: in the second cabin layout the forward galley moves one frame aft and two rows that need the long hose are not on the list built from the first layout. A short hose on either of those rows gives a start-of-sequence flow below the acceptance figure, and nothing about the installation looks wrong, so the layout must be established before the aircraft is worked.
sections.material_note: Kit K3520-2002-01 is supplied per cabin and contains the generators, the hose set, the actuators and the clamp set. State the cabin layout on the kit order: the generator and actuator counts are the same for both layouts but the outboard hose count is not, and a kit ordered without the layout is built to the first layout by default. Lead time is twenty-four weeks and the generator is the long-lead item. Removed generators are not returned and must be discharged and disposed of by the operator.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience, and before the operator plans a route whose depressurisation escape profile exceeds twelve minutes.

revision_history.reason: Outboard hose row list split by cabin layout; cabin layout added as an input to the kit order and to the embodiment record
